close_reason: Fixed in bf895d2: added pub const PROP_CREATED, PROP_UPDATED, PROP_NAME_GIVEN, PROP_NAME_SURNAME, PROP_NAME_SURNAME2 in a new card::prop module (re-exported as comparator_prop) for spelling-safe call sites. The property field remains String to preserve forward-compat with vendor sort keys and future RFC additions per the workspace filter-algebra exclusion (JMAP-lbdy).
description:
ContactCardComparator.property (card.rs:330) holds the sort-key string.
RFC 9610 §3.3.2 declares a small required + recommended set:
- Required: "created", "updated"
- Recommended: "name/given", "name/surname", "name/surname2"

Current type:

```rust
pub struct ContactCardComparator {
    pub property: String,    // <-- free string, no constraint
    ...
}
```

A caller writing `comparator.property = "name/givien".into()` compiles,
serializes, deserializes, and silently sorts wrong (the backend either
rejects with an error or — worse — falls through to a default
comparator, returning a result set the caller cannot tell is wrong).

The workspace filter-algebra exclusion (correctly applied here via the
rustdoc clause referencing bd JMAP-lbdy, lines 315-324) blocks the
typed-enum route: adding `Other(String)` on a comparator property is
incoherent because the backend cannot honor an unknown sort key. But
the exclusion policy does NOT require the type to be a naked String
with zero helpers.

Minimum-viable improvement: expose pub const string identifiers for the
spec values, making typos a compile error:

```rust
impl ContactCardComparator {
    pub const PROP_CREATED:        &str = "created";
    pub const PROP_UPDATED:        &str = "updated";
    pub const PROP_NAME_GIVEN:     &str = "name/given";
    pub const PROP_NAME_SURNAME:   &str = "name/surname";
    pub const PROP_NAME_SURNAME2:  &str = "name/surname2";
}
```

Then callers write:

```rust
ContactCardComparator {
    property: ContactCardComparator::PROP_NAME_GIVEN.into(),
    is_ascending: true,
    collation: None,
}
```

Typos surface as `error[E0599]: no associated item named PROP_NAME_GIVIEN`.

The same gap applies to known-enumeration `Option<String>` filter fields:
- `filter.kind` (RFC 9553 §2.1.1: "individual"|"group"|"org"|"location"|
  "device"|"application")
- `filter.collation` (the comparator field, RFC 4790 registry)

Note: this is **complementary** to the filter-exclusion policy, not in
conflict with it. The policy excludes typed enums with `Other(String)`
on the comparator algebra; it does not exclude const helper strings.

Cross-reference: AGENTS.md §"Filter algebra and control enums are
explicitly EXCLUDED" — confirms typed enum is wrong; const pool is
silent on this and therefore allowed.
title: ContactCardComparator.property is a free String with no validator, no const pool, no parse method
